title: Learning Molecular Chirality via Chiral Determinant Kernels
claim: Chirality arises from the spatial arrangement of key atoms and appears in both simple central and more complex axial forms.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right, mirror-image pairs with a central enantiomer icon
description: Two rounded gray panels, (a) central chirality and (b) axial chirality. Each panel has a pair of 2D skeletal molecular structures. The left structure sits in a blue rounded box and the right one in an orange rounded box. A small mirror icon with a hand sits between them to show that they are enantiomers, meaning mirror images. In (a), an amino acid-like molecule has a green circle on the chiral carbon and yellow circles on the surrounding chiral-related atoms. The wedge and dashed bonds flip between the two structures. In (b), a biaryl-like pyrrole-phenyl molecule has the green highlight on the C–N axis and yellow highlights on the flanking substituents. A legend at the bottom explains green for chiral atoms, yellow for chiral-related atoms, and the mirror icon for enantiomers. The eye goes first to the colored molecule boxes.
caption: Examples of central chirality (a) and axial chirality (b). The configuration of the chiral atoms (in green) is determined by the spatial arrangement of chiral-related atoms (in orange).
abstract: Chirality is a fundamental molecular property that governs stereospecific behavior in chemistry and biology. Capturing chirality in machine learning models remains challenging due to the geometric complexity of stereochemical relationships and the limitations of traditional molecular representations that often lack explicit stereochemical encoding. Existing approaches to chiral molecular representation primarily focus on central chirality, relying on handcrafted stereochemical tags or limited 3D encodings, and thus fail to generalize to more complex forms such as axial chirality. In this work, we introduce ChiDeK (Chiral Determinant Kernels), a framework that systematically integrates stereogenic information into molecular representation learning. We propose the chiral determinant kernel to encode the SE(3)-invariant chirality product and employ cross-attention to integrate stereochemical information from local chiral centers into the global molecular representation. This design enables explicit modeling of chiral-related features within a unified architecture, capable of jointly encoding central and axial chirality. To support the evaluation of axial chirality, we construct a new benchmark for electronic circular dichroism (ECD) and optical rotation (OR) prediction. Across four tasks, including R/S configuration classification, enantiomer ranking, ECD spectrum prediction, and OR prediction, ChiDeK achieves substantial improvements over state-of-the-art baselines, most notably yielding over 7% higher accuracy on axially chiral tasks on average.
